messages:
Anya Patel: Kicking off POC scoping for Acme — need a concise prompt inventory + baseline prompt set for a 2-week pilot. Constraints: EU data residency, budget cap ~$12k, acceptance criteria: hallucination rate <5% on eval set, p95 latency <300ms, throughput ~50 rps. Who can own the inventory?

Jordan Lee: I can own the inventory. Quick clarifying Q: will we try Hosted API first (fast) or go Dedicated from day 1? Pricing delta affects the budget.

Anya Patel: Prefer Hosted to start, but if data residency or KMS locks us we might need Dedicated. @Leila Gomez can you confirm whether EU KMS + no-external-logging is mandatory?

Leila Gomez: EU KMS is required for this customer. Security questionnaire also flagged 'no external logging' and 'audit trail retention policy'. We can disable request logging in the Hosted environment for the POC but legal wants a signed DPA before prod. I'll drop SQA answers to the doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/EXAMPLE_LINK

Sam Ortiz: For a baseline model I'd suggest we test two variants: a cost-optimized open-7b quantized and a higher-quality redwood-rlhf-1. Baseline prompt families: (A) single-turn summarization, (B) multi-turn action extraction, (C) structured extraction (JSON). Target eval set ~200 examples covering edge cases (ambiguous ask, long context, contradictory statements). Also add a small adversarial set for hallucination checks. Sample baseline prompt (copyable):

```
Prompt: "Given the customer conversation, produce a short summary, 3 recommended next actions (prioritized), and a confidence score between 0 and 1. Output MUST be valid JSON with keys: summary, actions, confidence."
Input tag: <customer_conversation>
Max tokens: 150
Temperature: 0.0
Output format: JSON
```

Jordan Lee: Good. Add an explicit negative-class section to the eval (i.e., cases where model should return "no_answer" or "insufficient_info"). Also, assume ~200 tokens/request average for cost projection.

Anya Patel: Proposed timeline: inventory + sample prompts by Tue (48h), curated eval set by Fri, test run (first automated pass) next Monday. Owners: Jordan = inventory + cost estimate, Sam = prompt baseline + eval harness, Leila = security sign-off + SQA answers.

Anya Patel: @redwood-deploy-bot can you create a POC workspace and grant Jordan & Sam access (they need access to the customer sandbox and token controls)?

redwood-deploy-bot: Created workspace "poc-acme-171772" and granted access to @Jordan Lee, @Sam Ortiz. Workspace has logging disabled and EU KMS flag set. :rocket:

Leila Gomez: Note for Legal: DPA required before we escalate to Dedicated or production. Also confirm whether customer requires HSM-backed keys — if so, lead time is ~2 weeks.

Sam Ortiz: I'll draft 3 prompt variants per family (concise, context-rich, instruction-heavy) and attach an eval harness (pytest-based runner + small runner script). Example eval command I plan to include:

```
pytest tests/evals/test_hallucination.py -k smoke
python tools/eval_runner.py --model redwood-rlhf-1 --dataset datasets/acme_eval.json --out results.json
```

Jordan Lee: I'll populate the inventory sheet with sample prompts, expected outputs, failure modes, and token estimates. I'll also add a cost projection for Hosted vs Dedicated for the two model families.

Anya Patel: Great — once we have first-pass cost + security answers we can give Sales a clean one-pager: scope, timeline, success criteria, and estimated cost. Daily async updates in this thread please. :thumbsup:

Jordan Lee: On it. First pass in the shared sheet by EOD today.

Sam Ortiz: Draft prompts and initial eval harness uploaded to the workspace. Will iterate after Jordan's inventory.

Anya Patel: Thanks everyone — this should unblock pre-sales. Jordan: confirm hosted cost estimate by Wed so Sales can push the SOW.

Jordan Lee: Will confirm Wed.

Leila Gomez: Pinged Legal for DPA. Will update here when signed.

Anya Patel: Closing notes: owners + deliverables repeated in the sheet. Short daily standups optional — prefer async updates here.
